# GX001 game-coverage-undeclared

A project with a `[game]` profile declares every game accessibility coverage key. Each block is
one source file in a project whose `crunk.toml` is the default preset plus a `[game]` table; the
case's `config` selects which coverage keys it declares.

## What it does

For a project with a `[game]` table, requires `coverage` to name every key: `volume_channels`
(separate music, effects and speech volume), `haptics_toggle` (haptics can be turned off),
`time_limits` (adjustable or removable, up to 10x), `subtitle_format` (at most 2 lines, 38 to 40
characters per line), `text_in_images` (no essential text baked into images) and `glyph_icons`
(Unicode glyph icons carry a text alternative). Each missing key is one finding that names the
guideline (GAG, XAG, IGDA). A project without `[game]` is not judged.

## Why it matters

Each item has two or more voices among the Game Accessibility Guidelines, the Xbox Accessibility
Guidelines and the IGDA GA-SIG; a game that has not said how it handles them has not decided.

## Remedy

Declare the key in `[game] coverage = [...]` once the project handles it, or waive the rule with a
reason.

## Examples

### A game profile with no volume channel declaration fires

```css expect=fire config=game-no-volume file=styles/app.css
.a {
  margin: 0;
}
```

### A game profile declaring every key is clean

```css expect=clean config=game-complete file=styles/app.css
.a {
  margin: 0;
}
```
